get.description:
Lightweight liveness endpoint.

This endpoint only proves that the FastAPI process is running.

It does NOT check:
- PostgreSQL
- Redis
- MinIO / S3
- tenant databases
- external integrations

Intended for:
- Docker liveness checks
- Kubernetes liveness probes
- reverse proxy checks

Check whether WorkforceOS is ready to serve requests.

Required infrastructure:
- control PostgreSQL database
- Redis
- MinIO / S3

HTTP status:
    200 -> ready
    503 -> not ready

Return detailed WorkforceOS infrastructure health.

Includes:
- overall status
- environment
- application version
- process uptime
- database health
- Redis health
- object-storage health
- latency for each dependency

HTTP behavior:
    healthy  -> 200
    degraded -> 200
    unhealthy -> 503

A degraded system may still be partially operational,
therefore degraded does not automatically return 503.

Create a signed Google OAuth authorization URL.

The frontend should navigate the browser to
authorization_url returned by this endpoint.

Exchange Google's authorization code and authenticate the
corresponding global WorkforceOS user.

Google provider tokens are never returned to the frontend.

get.description:
List devices in the already-authorized tenant.

Authorized workspace members may read device inventory.
Read one device from the authorized tenant.

patch.description:
Administrative device update.

Lifecycle transition to revoked also revokes tenant-side
credentials through DeviceService.

delete.description:
Revoke a registered endpoint across tenant and control planes.

Sequence:

    authorized tenant lookup
        ↓
    resolve trusted device_uuid
        ↓
    revoke Device + credentials in tenant DB
        ↓
    revoke DeviceRoute in control DB

Hard deletion is intentionally avoided so historical monitoring
and audit records remain attributable to the endpoint.

Assign or unassign a device.

employee_id=None explicitly removes the assignment.

post.description:
First-time endpoint enrollment endpoint.

Expected client payload:

    activation_code
    hostname
    os_name
    os_version
    architecture
    agent_version
    agent_identifier

The endpoint deliberately accepts no:

    workspace_id
    tenant_id
    database_name
    database_url
    cluster_key
    device_uuid
    employee_id
    monitoring_profile_id

Successful registration returns:

    Device information
    server-generated device_uuid
    one-time device_secret

The plaintext device_secret is generated during enrollment,
returned once, and is not stored plaintext by the backend.

get.description:
List safe credential metadata for one device.

Plaintext secrets and secret hashes are never returned.

delete.description: Revoke every currently active credential for a device.

post.description:
Revoke currently active credential(s) and issue a replacement.

The new plaintext device secret is returned exactly once.

delete.description: Revoke one credential belonging to this device.

get.description:
Verify device credentials and return the endpoint's safe
authenticated identity.

Authentication is performed by AuthenticatedDevice dependency:

    X-Device-UUID
    X-Device-Secret
        ↓
    DeviceRoute
        ↓
    trusted workspace
        ↓
    trusted tenant database
        ↓
    DeviceCredential
        ↓
    tenant Device

This response intentionally does not expose:

    workspace_id
    tenant database name
    cluster key
    credential_id
    secret hash
    device secret

post.description:
Record one authenticated WorkforceOS Agent heartbeat.

Device identity and tenant routing come exclusively from
authenticated device credentials.

get.description:
Return server-derived online/offline presence for the
currently authenticated device.

post.summary: Report authenticated device active or idle state
post.description:
Record one active/idle observation from an authenticated
WorkforceOS Agent.

Device identity and tenant routing are derived exclusively from
authenticated device credentials.

The request body cannot select:
- workspace
- tenant database
- device UUID
- employee assignment

No keystrokes, typed text, clipboard contents, or input content
are accepted by this endpoint.

After the activity event is persisted, the same tenant session
processes that event into the device's current work session.

get.summary: Get authenticated device current activity status
get.description:
Return the latest active/idle state for the currently
authenticated device.

This endpoint is agent-authenticated and is not intended to be
called by the web dashboard.

post.description:
Record the foreground application observed by an authenticated
WorkforceOS Agent.

Device and tenant identity are derived exclusively from the
authenticated device credential.

This endpoint does not accept keystrokes, clipboard content,
passwords, mouse coordinates, or typed input.

get.summary: Get authenticated device foreground application status

post.description:
Record one website/domain observation.

Security properties:

- device identity comes from authenticated credentials
- tenant selection comes from trusted server routing
- request cannot choose workspace/database
- request cannot choose device UUID
- employee identity is not accepted from the agent

Privacy defaults:

- domain is retained
- full URL is suppressed
- page title is suppressed
- query strings are never retained here

get.summary: Get authenticated device current website status
get.description:
Return the currently open website interval belonging to
the authenticated endpoint.

This is an agent diagnostic endpoint.

Browser dashboard/admin clients should not use device secrets.
A separate browser-facing aggregation API will be added in the
Platform/Core SaaS phase.

Return recent website/domain usage intervals belonging only
to the authenticated device.

DeviceRegistrationRequest.title: DeviceRegistrationRequest
DeviceRegistrationRequest.description:

DeviceRegistrationResponse.title: DeviceRegistrationResponse

credential.device_secret is plaintext and must be persisted
securely by the installed agent immediately.

The backend stores only the secret hash, so the plaintext
secret cannot be retrieved again later.

WorkspaceProvisioningResponse.title: WorkspaceProvisioningResponse
WorkspaceProvisioningResponse.description:
Public API response for workspace tenant provisioning.

This model deliberately exposes only safe provisioning state.

It never exposes:

- database credentials
- database URLs
- database host
- database port
- PostgreSQL username
- PostgreSQL password

database_name is intentionally not exposed through this
public API response. The physical tenant database identity
remains a server-side routing concern.
